title: Quadrotor Design and Control
description: CS/ME 410: built a quadrotor's entire flight stack in C over ten weeks — from raw IMU registers to a vehicle that holds its own position under an overhead camera.
highlights: Complementary filter fusing accelerometer and gyro for drift-free attitude
Tuned PID control on pitch, roll and yaw with full safety interlocks
Piloted hover in and out of ground effect
Autonomous yaw, x/y and altitude hold from ArUco camera tracking

title: UL Battery Drop Tester
description: Senior Mechanical Engineering Capstone, sponsored by UL Solutions: a remotely actuated battery drop tester that replaces the manual apparatus at UL's Small Battery Test Center, fully isolating the operator while delivering repeatable face, edge, and corner drops with adjustable height.
highlights: Six-person Northwestern ME Capstone team, sponsored by UL Solutions, over two quarters
Pneumatic piston release & orientation mechanism with motorized lead-screw height adjustment
RF remote actuation fully isolating the operator from the test environment
Achieved reliable drops across all three battery configurations — flat, edge, and corner

title: Titan Rotor/Airfoil CFD Studies
description: Set up RANS CFD for Titan atmosphere propeller/airfoil studies; computed Reynolds numbers, validated against literature, and compared to experimental trends.
highlights: Meshing strategy & y+ control
Post-processing scripts for lift/drag

title: NASA Student Launch: Active Drag System
description: Wind tunnel testing for the NUSTARS Active Drag System on Northwestern's 2025 NASA Student Launch competition rocket, mapping actuation states to drag coefficients.
highlights: Mapped ADS actuation states to drag coefficients through wind tunnel testing
Optimized a 16-hour test schedule to maximize design points
Swept velocity up to Mach 0.31, angle of attack, and actuation state
Analyzed CFD vs. empirical discrepancies to inform future simulations

title: NASA Big Idea Challenge: METALS
description: Advanced the development of inflatable metal systems for lunar infrastructure through innovative Free Inner Pressure Deformation (FIDU) technology.
highlights: Received $146,000 funding as one of six finalist schools
Developed inflatable metal systems for lunar infrastructure
Optmized the geometry of the inflatables for stress optimization
Manufactured 50+ inflatables with various materials and shapes
Received the ARTEMIS Award as top prize in the Challenge

title: Mechanical Design and Manufacturing: ME240
description: Designed and tested a solenoid-actuated robot arm end effector that lifts an egg without breaking it, iterating with CAD, FEA, and physical load testing.
highlights: Redesigned static and actuated components for a TinkerKit Braccio arm
Reconciled FEA against physical testing when the two disagreed
Reduced part weight across design iterations
Evaluated PLA as a lower-emission alternative to SLS Nylon 12
